key_insight: E-RLBM independently relaxes nonhydrodynamic modes to tune stability and higher-order errors while preserving Navier–Stokes viscosity and interpolating between BGK and regularized collision operators.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a low-cost way to expand stable lattice Boltzmann operating ranges without implementing a full multiple-relaxation-time basis.
method: Separate nonequilibrium distributions into second-order hydrodynamic and complementary kinetic sectors.
Apply distinct relaxation times to the two sectors using a two-rate collision operator.
Analyze viscosity and direction-dependent fourth-order shear errors, then evaluate stability and convergence.
evidence_signal: Taylor–Green vortex and obstacle-flow tests show enlarged stable domains; Taylor–Green convergence remains second order, with E-RLBM error about 6% above BGK and 40% below RLBM, while a Re = 80,000 double shear layer follows RLBM convergence.
watch_item: Kinetic relaxation changes direction-dependent higher-order errors, so improved stability does not guarantee improved accuracy over BGK.
